Braintree's population increased by around 8,200 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 160,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Braintree increased by 5.6%, from around 147,100 in 2011 to around 155,300 in 2021.

The population here increased by a smaller percentage than the overall population of the East of England (8.3%), and by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Braintree was home to around 1.8 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 1.7 in 2011. This area was among the lowest 30% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in Braintree than across the East of England

An older Braintree

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Braintree increased by two years, from 41 to 43 years of age.

This area had a higher average (median) age than the East of England as a whole in 2021 (41 years) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 65 to 74 years rose by just under 4,400 (an increase of 33.5%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by just over 3,500 (10.6% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 65 and 74 years increased by 2.3 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Change in housing in Braintree

Of Braintree households, 67.8% owned their home in 2021, down from 68.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in seven households (15.1%) rented privately, compared with 13.2% in 2011. The percentage of Braintree households that lived in a socially rented property decreased from 16.5% to 16.3%.

The decrease in the percentage of households that owned their home was greater across the East of England (2.4 percentage points, from 67.6% to 65.2%) than in Braintree (0.7 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 2.0 percentage points, from 63.3% to 61.3%.

The rate of home ownership in Braintree decreased by 0.7 percentage points

Unpaid care in Braintree

In 2021, 4.4% of Braintree residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.3% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Braintree (2.9 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the East of England (2.8 percentage points, from 7.3% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Braintree decreased by 2.9 percentage points

Religion in Braintree

In 2021, 45.0% of Braintree residents reported having "No religion", up from 30.0% in 2011. The rise of 15.0 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Braintree. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the East of England, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.9% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 47.1% of people in Braintree described themselves as Christian (down from 61.3%), while 5.9% did not state their religion (down from 7.1% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

In 2021, 45.0% of usual residents in Braintree reported having "No religion"

Braintree residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 141,400 Braintree residents said they were born in England. This represented 91.1% of the local population. The figure has risen from just over 135,300 in 2011, which at the time represented 92.0% of Braintree's population.

Poland was the next most represented, with just under 1,500 Braintree residents reporting this country of birth (0.9%). This figure was up from around 1,400 in 2011, which at the time also represented 0.9% of the population of Braintree.

The number of Braintree residents born in Scotland fell from around 1,700 in 2011 (1.2% of the local population) to just under 1,500 in 2021 (0.9%).

In 2021, 91.1% of Braintree residents reported their country of birth as England

Lone parents in Braintree

In 2021, 9.9% of Braintree households included a lone parent. This figure was at a similar level in 2011 (9.8%).

The percentage of lone-parent households increased from 9.4% to 10.2% across the East of England. Across England, the percentage increased from 10.6% to 11.1%.

The percentage of households including a lone parent in Braintree increased by 0.1 percentage points

National identity in Braintree

In 2021, 4.0% of Braintree residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 3.5% in 2011.

In 2021, 1.0% of residents identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.5% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Braintree that identified as "British only" increased from 13.8% to 54.8%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across the East of England (2.1 percentage points, from 6.9% to 9.0%) than in Braintree (0.4 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Braintree increased by 0.4 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Braintree residents aged 16 years and over, 32.9% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 28.8% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in two people (48.6%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 51.8% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Braintree that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 9.9% to 10.2%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership in Braintree (4.0 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the East of England (3.7 percentage points, from 31.1% to 34.8%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Braintree increased by 4.0 percentage points

Change in employment

Of Braintree residents aged 16 years and over, 59.1% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, down from 61.3% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 40 people (2.4%) said they were unemployed, compared with 3.4% in 2011. The percentage of retired Braintree residents increased from 21.6% to 23.6%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater in Braintree (2.2 percentage points) than across the East of England (1.1 percentage points, from 58.4% to 57.3%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.8 percentage points, from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Braintree decreased by 2.2 percentage points

Change in work hours

In 2021, 11.3% of Braintree residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 10.3% in 2011.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week was greater in Braintree (1.0 percentage points) than across the East of England (0.4 percentage points, from 10.4% to 10.8%). Across England, the percentage increased by 0.6 percentage points, from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Braintree increased by 1.0 percentage points

Disability in Braintree

In 2021, 6.6% of Braintree residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 7.8% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just over 1 in 10 people (10.2%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 9.7% in 2011. The proportion of Braintree residents who were not disabled increased from 82.5% to 83.2%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Braintree (1.2 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the East of England (1.2 percentage points, from 7.8% to 6.6%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Braintree decreased by 1.2 percentage points

Health in Braintree

In 2021, 47.4% of Braintree residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 45.9% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 36.3% to 35.7%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Braintree residents describing their health as "very bad" was 0.9% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 3.6% to 3.4%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Braintree increased by 1.5 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Braintree

In 2021, 1.9% of Braintree residents identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category, up from 1.2% in 2011. The 0.7 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the East of England, the percentage of people from "Mixed or Multiple ethnic groups" increased from 1.9% to 2.8%, while across England the percentage increased from 2.3% to 3.0%.

In 2021, 94.7% of people in Braintree identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 96.6% in 2011), while 1.7% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (compared with 1.4% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category increased from 0.6% in 2011 to 1.2% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.
